step3_verification.method: for each of the 5 reported lives_candidates (11, 142, 9, 176, 340): (a) read true root value under 150 pure-NOOP steps; (b) trace every value change across all 5 death-drive rollouts (700 steps each) and its offset from the run's own mass-RAM-rewrite (reload/death) events
step3_verification.finding: NONE of the 5 candidates -- nor the 3 further same-shaped candidates visible when the rank cutoff is widened past top=6 (addr 1942=6, 2039=7, 1909=8) -- behave like a real stock. Two failure shapes: (A) addr 11 (root=0), addr 9 (root=0), addr 176 (root=4) FREE-RUN: 15-38 value changes across a single 700-step drive, oscillating repeatedly through 0/low-value/255, uncorrelated with any mass-RAM-rewrite (death/reload) event. (B) addr 142 (root=2) and addr 340 (root=5) dip to 0 and INSTANTLY (1-8 frames later) recover to their exact original baseline in every one of 5 runs, 2-4 times per 700-step run -- most of these dip/recover pairs do not line up with the run's own mass-RAM-rewrite timestamp at all (only 1 of ~3-4 dips per candidate per run falls near an actual reload), and addr 340 additionally passes through a nonsense intermediate value (55) mid-transition on 3 of 5 runs -- not a lives byte draining or a level reload, more consistent with a transient hit-flash/animation-cycle timer.
step3_verification.cross_family_pattern: addr 11, 142, 9, 176, 340, 1942, 2039, 1909 form ONE family: start values 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 respectively, IDENTICAL statistical signature (5/5 agree, spends=5, refilled_runs=5, reaches_empty=True, spends_its_stock=True), and mostly-sequential mirror addresses clustering at 2031/2033-2040 (top of the 2KB internal RAM). This is the signature of ONE shared periodic RAM-clear/redraw effect (plausibly an OAM-shadow or attribute-row blank-then-redraw tied to the Niagara level's mist/waterfall animation) hitting several unrelated RAM cells simultaneously, not eight independent life stocks. discover_observables.py's structural checks (reaches_empty / spends_its_stock / 5-of-5 agreement) cannot distinguish 'drained to empty by a death' from 'blanked to 0 for a few frames by an unrelated redraw and then restored,' because both look identical inside a single 700-step window with no requirement that the recovery coincide with an actual level-reload event.
step3_verification.verdict: NO CANDIDATE VERIFIES. The #1 rank (0x000B itself) is provably the same false byte the task set out to replace, still on top after the fix, for a reason adjacent to (not a recurrence of) the fixed bug. The next four ranks are equally spurious for an unrelated reason (shared periodic redraw artifact).
